vedic_reference.note: Rajeev is a name derived from the Sanskrit word राजीव (rājīva), which means 'king of passion' or 'ruler of desire'. In Hindu mythology, Rajeev is also associated with Lord Vishnu, who is often depicted as the ruler of all desires. The name is considered auspicious and is used for boys in various parts of India.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rajeev holds great cultural significance in India, where it is associated with royalty, power, and authority. The name is derived from the sanskrit word 'raja' which means king. Historically, names with the root 'raja' were given to those who held positions of power and authority within Hindu society. Today, the name Rajeev continues to be popular in India and among the Indian diaspora around the world, and is often given to babies who are expected to one day hold positions of power, leadership, and influence.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rajeev carries the resonance of the inner king or inner ruler within each of us. Just as a monarch rules over a kingdom, the inner ruler or atman rules over the mind and the body. The name Rajeev also reminds us of the ultimate reality of consciousness, that we are all divine kings of our own soul and consciousness. Therefore, the name Rajeev can serve as a powerful reminder of the spiritual kingdom within us and the deep inner power and authority that we all possess.
